item.title: Nepal’s Real state Multi-Millionaire: Future | Scams |Policy | Money | Satakshi Mishra|
item.description:
Co-Founder of Skill Sewa, Satakshi has been contributing to Nepal’s construction and real estate sector by providing professional services, including home inspections, construction-related solutions, and property services. What began with just four employees has grown into an organization employing hundreds of people directly and creating opportunities for thousands more through indirect and part-time employment.
Skill Sewa is Nepal’s first home inspection company, offering a wide range of services, including interior design, renovation, construction, house design, waterproofing, and more. Here’s why Skill Sewa is your one-stop solution for home improvement. They have also introduced several new ventures, including the White Room and Colony concepts.
Her journey reflects the importance of creating opportunities rather than simply waiting for them. Instead of limiting herself to traditional career expectations, she stepped into an industry where she saw room for improvement and innovation.

item.title: Digital sovereignty secretly manipulating ? |Power|System| Politics| Gen-z| Priya Sigdel |
item.description:
In this episode of Thinking Beyond Podcast, we sit down with Priya Sigdel, associated with Miss Nepal Earth 2018, for a thought-provoking conversation about her experiences, ambition, personal growth, and the realities of Nepali society.
The founder of HattiHatti. From overcoming rejection and understanding the hunger for success to discussing women’s empowerment, superstition, and the challenges women face, we explore the ideas that shape individuals and communities. We also dive into Nepal’s political future, digital governance, government accountability, youth responsibility, and how Nepal can build a stronger digital identity.
We discuss maturity, fear, mistakes, regrets, comfort zones, and why meaningful growth often begins when we challenge ourselves and question conventional thinking.

item.title: Can Nepal Build a Unicorn? | Truth Behind Nepali Startup Ecosystem Nobody Talks | NJ Subedi |
item.description:
NJ Subedi’s journey is an inspiring example of how self-learning, experimentation, and persistence can turn ideas into successful businesses. After stepping away from college, he pursued his entrepreneurial ambitions.Through Yarsa Games, the company entered the global mobile gaming industry, reaching millions of users and demonstrating that products developed in Nepal can succeed internationally.
But his vision extends beyond gaming. Through Yarsa Tech, NJ is working toward expanding Nepal’s electronics and hardware manufacturing capabilities, with the ambition of creating technology products locally rather than relying heavily on imports
However, building technology businesses in Nepal comes with significant challenges, including high operating costs, taxes on imported components, limited payment infrastructure, and difficulties protecting intellectual property. NJ has called for policy reforms to reduce unnecessary costs, support IT exports, improve access to international payment systems, and create a more business-friendly environment for Nepali technology companies. His journey raises an important question: Can Nepal become a country that not only consumes technology but also builds and exports it to the world?

item.title: The Unseen Battle Behind the 400 Cr Empire |Ten Group|Adversity |Trust Building|
item.description:
In this episode, We sat down with Dheeraj kumar Agrawal. No degree. No safety net. Today, Dhiraj Kumar Agarwal, founder of Ten Group, runs a Rs 400 crore business empire in Nepal. Most people would have given up.
Dhiraj turned to the one thing the accident couldn't take from him: his mind. Starting in hardware in 2011, he built from zero, with no academic strength to lean on, only courage and a refusal to let adversity define him. Over the years, that mindset grew into one of Nepal's biggest business stories.In this conversation, he goes back to the beginning: the accident, the self-doubt, the people who underestimated him, the risks that could have ended everything, and how he built an empire with his mind.

item.title: Are Women Safe In Nepal? Dr Renu Adhikari | Rape|Sexual Violence| Nepal Police-Institutional Failure
item.description:
Dr. Renu Adhikari, founder of WOREC and women’s rights activist, reveals why women still face violence, harassment and insecurity in Nepal—and what society, institutions and the law are failing to address.
She explains: ◼ Are women actually safe in Nepal—? ◼ Who is responsible when rape happens—the perpetrator, society, institutions, or a system that fails to protect survivors? ◼ Why stricter laws alone may not be enough—and where Nepal’s justice system and institutions are failing ◼ What should actually happen when a rape or sexual violence case is reported—and how survivors should be supported ◼ What high-profile cases reveal about the gap between Nepal’s laws, institutions and reality.
item.itunes:subtitle: Dr. Renu Adhikari, founder of WOREC and women’s rights activist, reveals why women still face violence, harassment and insecurity in Nepal—and what society, institutions and the law are failing to address.

item.title: Rekha Yadav (Finance awareness creator) |Stock Market| Author
item.description:
Today’s guest is Rekha Yadav , She had a double degree in Economics and Finance, a stable job at Siddhartha Bank — and she walked away from it all to bet on herself.
In this episode of Thinking Beyond, we sit down with a young entrepreneur from Janakpur who turned financial uncertainty into financial freedom. From learning to trade on NEPSE to building a personal brand around financial awareness, her journey is proof that small-town beginnings don't limit big ambitions.
Today, she is a stock market trader and financial awareness content creator, brand ambassador for three national and international companies, founder of her own IT company, and owner of her own clothing brand — living proof that leaving the "safe path" can lead somewhere far bigger. In this conversation, we talk about the fear of quitting a secure job, learning to trade from scratch, building multiple businesses at once, and what it really takes to go from a small town in Janakpur to national recognition. If you've ever doubted whether you can build something of your own, this episode is for you.
item.itunes:subtitle: Today’s guest is Rekha Yadav , She had a double degree in Economics and Finance, a stable job at Siddhartha Bank — and she walked away from it all to bet on herself.

item.title: Nepali Gym Industry Is Selling You a Lie? | Shivani Lama | Belly Fat Burn-Sceince-Myths
item.description:
In this episode of Thinking Beyond, we sit down with Shivani Lama — Fitness Coach & Athlete Trainer — to break down the real science behind fitness, fat loss and nutrition.
From protein, sugar, calories and belly fat to cardio, strength training and the reality of the Nepali diet, we separate science from fitness myths.
We also explore what research actually says about high-protein diets, obesity, lifestyle diseases, fat loss and sustainable fitness — and what truly matters beyond simply spending more time in the gym.
item.itunes:subtitle: In this episode of Thinking Beyond, we sit down with Shivani Lama — Fitness Coach & Athlete Trainer — to break down the real science behind fitness, fat loss and nutrition.

item.title: Ashima Poudyal (Into Aroma) 9-5 job into entrepreneurship | Failure | Mindset | Nepal |
item.description: What happens when you choose entrepreneurship over the “safe” 9–5path? In this episode of Thinking Beyond, we sit down with Ashima Poudel to unpack her journey from a conventional 9–5 career to building her own brand and stepping into entrepreneurship. We talk about the reality of building a business in Nepal — the mindset, failures, uncertainty, financial pressure, and the moments when giving up feels easier than continuing. From being told “you’ll be nobody if you want to be an entrepreneur” to choosing to build anyway, Ashima shares the lessons, struggles and decisions that shaped her journey
